codemap:
# Codemap — issue 0150, corpus invariant for children declared on an entryLink

Files this issue has to change. Paths are repo-relative to /home/user/tome_of_battle.

## The check itself (new)

- `src/evaluator/<new>.test.js` — new file holding the corpus invariant; it has to live under `src/evaluator/` because criterion 5 requires it to run with `npx vitest run src/evaluator`. Exact name is the researcher's call; the suite's naming convention is in `src/evaluator/CLAUDE.md`.
- possibly a second new non-test module beside it (or under `scripts/lib/`) if the corpus derivation is worth pinning on its own — only if the researcher finds the derivation needs its own tests; not required by the issue.

## Read-only inputs of the check (not to be changed, listed so they are not searched for twice)

- `src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/` and `src/__fixtures__/whfb6/` — the two frozen corpora the 6328/149 counts were measured on.
- `src/evaluator/evaluator.js` — the facade the check may reach the engine through (`prepareDataset` + `evaluate`, re-exported from `datasetPreparation.js`); every other `src/evaluator/*.js` is off limits to the check per criteria 1 and ADR 0033.
- `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` §4.4 and the `Catalogue.xsd` it points at — the only source for what an `entryLink`'s own children mean.
- `src/evaluator/evalTree.linkLocalChildren.test.js` — the unit-level test PR #214 left behind for the same defect; the invariant must not duplicate it, and it shows what the engine now does.
- `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.js` — holds `CORPUS_DIRS`, `loadCorpus` and the corpus/testing paths; change it only if the check reuses it and needs an export it does not have today.

## Campaign bookkeeping

- `docs/testing/covered-cells.json` — criterion 6: gains the entry recording what the check attests. Its `_comment` defines what a manual entry is for.
- `docs/testing/worklist.json` — regenerated from `covered-cells.json` by `scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js`; the drift guard in `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.test.js` deep-equals the committed file, so any edit to `covered-cells.json` forces this file to change too.

## Campaign documentation

- `.claude/skills/evaluator-constraint-explorer/SKILL.md` — criterion 7: the loop's own instructions; it is what the campaign reads on every invocation, and it currently states the cell key and the covered-cells rules without any limit on what a cell measures.
- `docs/testkatalog-evaluator-e2e.md` — criterion 7 (the issue leaves the choice between this and the SKILL.md open, `and/or`): the campaign's long-form catalogue of what the E2E track covers.

## The issue file

- `docs/issues/0150-corpus-invariant-for-link-local-children/issue.md` — its empty `Plan` / `Tasks` / `Decisions` / `Log` / `Retro` sections are filled as the run proceeds; frontmatter `pr` is set when the pull request opens.

increments.title: The invariant, proven on the catalogue that shipped the defect
increments.goal: A check that derives from the corpus XML which entryLinks of one catalogue declare their own children, and asserts through the facade that a roster holding such a link gets a report slot for every locally declared child under the link's own slot — proven to go red on the pre-PR-#214 engine.
criteria: The check derives the entryLinks that declare their own selectionEntries, selectionEntryGroups or entryLinks from the catalogue XML alone, for at least the Empire (definitive) catalogue (31 occurrences), and asserts for each that a roster holding the link gets a report slot for each locally declared child under the link's own slot (issue criterion 1).

It reads only catalogue files, docs/battlescribe-data-format.md and Catalogue.xsd for its expectation, never any src/evaluator/*.js other than the facade, and reaches the engine only through prepareDataset + evaluate (issue criterion 1, ADR 0030, ADR 0033).
Existence is the assertion: the check asserts the slot is present and asserts nothing about isHidden (issue criterion 3).
The Captain -> Warhorse -> Barding link and the Captain -> Battle Standard Bearer -> Magic banners group are both among the occurrences the check covers (issue Log, third bullet).

The check is demonstrated red against an isolated revert of the ownerDefinitionOf change of PR #214 and green on the current tree, with the command, the revert used and both exit codes recorded (issue criterion 4).
npx vitest run src/evaluator passes and stays inside the suite's timeout.
increments.note: The load-bearing increment: whether a legal roster can be synthesised or found for an arbitrary link-carrying occurrence, and whether the report exposes the link's own slot in a way an outside observer can address, are the two open code facts of the whole issue. One catalogue first so both are answered before the corpus scale-up is committed to.

increments.title: All 149 occurrences, with every unreachable one accounted for
increments.goal: The check spans both corpora and all 15 catalogue files, and its books close: every occurrence it cannot assert is recorded with its reason, and recorded plus checked equals 149.
criteria: The check covers all 149 occurrences across the 15 catalogue files, in the per-file distribution the issue tabulates (issue criterion 2).

Any occurrence the check cannot assert — no roster can legally hold the link, or its carrier is not reachable from a force — is recorded with its reason instead of being silently skipped (issue criterion 2).
The recorded count plus the checked count equals 149, asserted by the check itself rather than stated in prose (issue criterion 2).
Each catalogue is prepared at most once per run, per the memoisation pattern src/evaluator/CLAUDE.md prescribes, and npx vitest run src/evaluator stays inside the suite's timeout (issue criterion 5).
increments.note: Scale-up of INC-1. Its own risks are distinct: cross-catalogue reachability, occurrences no roster can hold, and the runtime of parsing 15 catalogues in one suite run. The 149 figure was measured on the tree at PR #214 and is to be re-derived, not trusted.

increments.title: The campaign's books and its stated limit
increments.goal: The coverage bookkeeping records what the check attests, and the campaign's own documentation states in one sentence that the inventory measures rule constructs and not structural placements.
criteria: docs/testing/covered-cells.json gains an entry recording what this check attests, in the form that file's _comment provides for (issue criterion 6).
docs/testing/worklist.json is regenerated from the changed record and the drift guard in scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.test.js passes.

The campaign's documentation states the limit in one sentence — the inventory measures rule constructs, not structural placements, and this check covers the placement axis — placed where the loop reads it, in .claude/skills/evaluator-constraint-explorer/SKILL.md and/or docs/testkatalog-evaluator-e2e.md (issue criterion 7).
npm test, npm run lint and npm run typecheck are green, each reported with its command and exit code (issue criterion 8).
increments.note: Small but not mechanical: which key a covered-cells entry carries when what it attests is not a cell at all is an open decision, and the issue leaves the placement of the documented limit open with 'and/or'. Last, because what the entry attests is only settled once the check spans the corpus.

steps.label: decompose

return.summary: Issue 0150 is cut into three increments: the invariant proven on the Empire catalogue and demonstrated red against a revert of PR #214 (INC-1), the scale-up to all 149 occurrences with every unreachable one accounted for (INC-2), and the campaign's bookkeeping plus the stated limit of the cell inventory (INC-3). The codemap names the new check under src/evaluator/, the campaign records docs/testing/covered-cells.json and the worklist regenerated from it, and the two campaign documents.
